reply_text:
Thanks. I'll do the Zai token fix first, so this click has per-step token figures, then record renewal 8 and fire. Starting with how renewals are recorded and read.Renewals are recorded by adding a section to the renewal-7 document and raising `allocated` (47 → 48). I'll do that once the token fix is in. Now the Zai usage path.The terminal Agency job needs a `:usage` map. Next I'm finding where codex supplies one and where Zai's per-round counts live.I'm writing the Zai fix. Each turn will add up its per-round token counts and return the total as the job's `:usage`, which the WM run ledger already reads.Now writing the code and its test.Two syntax problems: one paren too many at the end of the loop, and `summary-result` isn't in scope where I used it. Fixing both.Lint is clean. Adding a test for a multi-round turn whose result carries summed usage.Loaded with no Zai seat mid-turn. Now checking it in the serving process: one tiny work turn on zai-4, which isn't in the click's cast, then reading the terminal job's `:usage`.Verified in the serving JVM. The probe job on zai-4 finished with `:usage` of 9,392 input (4,608 of them cached), 71 output, 2 calls, model glm-5.3. Committing, then recording the renewal.Now recording the renewal, following that document's own rule: add a section, then raise `allocated` from 47 to 48.Both parks are in place, pinned to my session, with a 6-hour deadline. Firing click 48.Joe, click 48 is running under the debugger.

**Firing details**
- Click `wm-click-28b44d70-08a9-4060-b174-a0c30ee27229`, run `2026-10-09-513e6445-4ce6-4bc4-a685-c5a5617a56de`, fired at 13:19:49 UTC.
- It's past budget admission (the ledger recorded the issue) and is in `substrate-preflight`.
- Cast: zai-1 author, zai-2 reviewer, zai-3 repair reviewer.
- The launcher runs detached from this session, so a restart of mine won't affect it. Its log is at `/tmp/c10/click48.log`.

**How I'll report back:** two parks, both pinned to this REPL session, each with a 6-hour deadline.
- `wm-debugger/stop`: wakes me at any debugger stop. I then follow A-self-heal: diagnose the stop, send one bounded repair to zai-4 with zai-5 reviewing, hot-load only after review, then `:retry` or `:abort`. I report each stop to you.
- `wm-click/end`: wakes me when the click finishes. I then report three things: the Lean requirements verdict (written to `<run-record>.requirements.edn` by `wm_run_alert.py`, which runs automatically); token spend per job and phase; and per-phase timing, with time held at debugger stops shown separately.

**Done before firing:**
- **Zai token counts** (futon3c `7498313b`, live): each Zai turn now returns its summed usage, so the job record carries tokens. I checked it in the running Agency process: a test turn on zai-4 recorded 9,392 input (4,608 cached), 71 output, 2 calls, glm-5.3. One limit: if a seat compacts its context before a turn, the tokens for that summary are only counted on newly registered seats. Seats that are already running still count every round of the turn itself.
- **Your grant** is recorded as a new section of the renewal-7 authorization document (futon2 `0d1e3ab7c`), with `allocated` raised to 48 (futon3c `a29246dc`, live).
- **Park signals** for click end and debugger stops are committed and live (futon3c `a6bfba52`). Two older runner-service tests also fail on a clean tree, so they aren't caused by this. The full runner-service suite hasn't completed a run.
